title: A letter from Wilno, 11 July 1757, on subsidies and the Strutyński affair (AGAD 1/338/0/1/131): read in part with the key of letter 446 by Prabal Gupta

documents.route: an unsigned writer ('manu notus', probably Matuszewicz) at Wilno -> a patron in the Branicki circle

plaintext.source: The ledger gives no reading; the contributor found no clear copy or decipherment of this letter, and compared letters 446, 1398, 1399 and 1400, which share titles but no passage.

transcription.source: the contributor's transcription of the five scans by Claude Opus 5.5, compared with a blind GPT-6.1 Sol pass (88% agreement on 2,514 tokens); about 300 differences are not settled on the scan; the project did not see the scans
transcription.notes: Look-alike signs (c, e and r; n, o and u; g and q; w and y); clear Polish in << >>.

system.summary: A reciprocal alphabet of twelve letter pairs plus a number code (the key of letter 446, unchanged); numbers from 830 up act as punctuation or nulls; the cipher parts are French inside clear Polish.

prior_solution.where: The ledger gives no reading; the contributor searched the ledger, the card and scans of the unit, and compared four sibling letters; Konopczyński (1909) and Matuszewicz's memoirs tell the affair but do not give this letter on the pages cited.

conditions.human_role: Prabal Gupta set the task and directed the work (issue #331, repository prabal-rje/branicki-1757); AI models (Claude, GPT) made the transcription passes and the reading. The key is his own key for letter 446. The project re-ran the decryption and a shuffled-key control; it has not seen the scans.

solution.what: Claude Opus 5.5 transcribed the letter from the five scans; a blind GPT-6.1 Sol pass agreed on 88% of 2,514 tokens; the hard lines were re-read on enlarged images; about 300 differences are not settled on the scan.
The key of letter 446 (target branicki1757) was applied with no change and read French; a count-matching fit on this letter alone gives the same key for 97.7% of letter tokens (contributor's figure).

The decryption was read as French inside clear Polish: about 25 of some 460 cipher words doubtful or holding an unread code; the group 190 and three signs stay unread; a blind reader named the cipher text French and three controls noise.
The contributor searched the ledger, the card and scans of the unit and compared letters 446, 1398, 1399 and 1400; Konopczyński (1909) and Matuszewicz's memoirs tell the affair but not this letter.

Project check: an own script applied the reciprocal key to the 64 cipher lines and got the contributor's decryption in 62 lines and at 99.9% letter agreement; a word-list test gives 46.3% of letters in listed words against a mean of 4.5% and a best of 19.1% for 200 shuffled keys (VERIFICATION.md). No scan compared.

Second check (14 Nov 2026, Brice Dudout with Claude; VERIFICATION.md section 4): own decoder from key.tsv alone, 2,447 of 2,449 letters as decryption.txt (the two differences are the capital X of p4.14 and p4.17, outside the key, given as K in decryption.txt). Recount by the README rule with v10_relabel.share: French cipher passages 576 words, 22 holes, 0.963 (whole file 0.971), replacing the estimate 0.946. Scans not seen; the contributor's ~300 pass differences remain unsettled.

Integration check of PR #559 (14 Nov 2026): own decoder from key.tsv gives 2,447 of 2,449 letters of decryption.txt (the two capital X); v10_relabel.share on reading.md: whole file 895 words, 27 holes (0.971); own paragraph split of the French cipher passages 563 words, 22 holes (0.962), against the contributor's 576/22 (0.963). Class kept read in part: word share above 0.95, but three signs and code 190 unread and the ~300 pass differences not settled on the scans.

validation.notes: The key is that of letter 446 applied unchanged; a word-list test against 200 shuffled keys was used instead of the project's n-gram test (VERIFICATION.md).

texts.label: Letter from Wilno, 11 July 1757 (AGAD 1/338/0/1/131)
texts.summary: An unsigned letter from Wilno of 11 July 1757 to a patron in the Branicki circle, in the contributor's reading: the Castellan of Brest and Count Pociej, Strażnik of Lithuania, ask protection and a subsidy for the coming Lithuanian Tribunal, having borrowed up to two hundred thousand francs beyond the French subsidy; the Castellan's nephew Ciechanowiecki's memorial is to go to the French ambassador, the Count de L'Hôpital; in the contributor's reading Strutyński, Starost of Szakinów, came armed to the Brasław dietine to kill a Ciechanowiecki (the word 'massacre' is a conjecture) and is shielded by Field Marshal Apraksin. The identities of writer and addressee and the two rumours at the end are the contributor's inference.

reading_review.note: Read the contributor's French and Polish as clauses: the clauses build coherent sentences with holes at unread codes and doubtful words; the names and events are the contributor's reading, not an edition.
